newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds end weaker, seen sliding further.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds end weaker, seen sliding further.

text.p: 1545 GMT - Austrian bonds were weaker on Thursday amid a growing belief that the German Bundesbank was unlikely to cut interest rates in the near future.
Further pressure from U.S. Treasuries which eased after a dip in jobless claims.
Traders see Austrian bonds heading lower short term.
"We were playing catch-up with Germany today. I don't see any news on the horizon that will turn the market around quickly," said one.
Light demand for the latest Austrian bond, maturing July 2006. The bond, issued on Tuesday, was indicated at 98.41/49 to yield 6.09/8 late afternoon.
* Benchmark 10-year 6.25 percent down 20 bps at 101.30 to yield 6.06 (6.03) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 101.14/24 to yield 6.08/07 percent.
* At the near end, five-year 5.25 percent bond maturing March 2001 down 20 bps at 102.30 to yield 4.93 (4.88) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 102.13/21 to yield 4.97/95 percent.
* 10-year spread to German bunds down two bps at five bps. Five-year spread down five bps at 22 bps.
* December AGB future down 18 bps at 105.50 on volume of 314 contracts.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR at 3.300 and overnight money at 1.00-08. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
